sources.title: LEVOCARNITINE injection, solution [U.S. FDA drug label, DailyMed]
sources.authors: U.S. Food and Drug Administration / DailyMed
quotes: For the prevention and treatment of carnitine deficiency in patients with end stage renal disease who are undergoing dialysis.
The recommended starting dose is 10 to 20 mg/kg dry body weight as a slow 2 to 3 minute bolus injection into the venous return line after each dialysis session.

End Stage Renal Disease (ESRD) patients on maintenance hemodialysis may have low plasma carnitine concentrations and an increased ratio of acylcarnitine/carnitine because of reduced intake of meat and dairy products, reduced renal synthesis and dialytic losses.
sources.notes: FDA-approved levocarnitine label: ESRD indication, dosing, dialytic-loss mechanism (scope a)

claims.claim: The FDA-approved label for levocarnitine injection covers the prevention and treatment of carnitine deficiency in patients with end-stage renal disease who are undergoing dialysis, with a recommended starting dose of 10 to 20 mg/kg dry body weight given intravenously into the venous return line after each dialysis session.
claims.quote: For the prevention and treatment of carnitine deficiency in patients with end stage renal disease who are undergoing dialysis.

claims.claim: Among 150 maintenance-dialysis patients, carnitine deficiency (serum free carnitine below 20 μmol/L) was present in 25.3% and carnitine insufficiency (acyl/free carnitine ratio above 0.4) in 86.7%.
claims.quote: The prevalence of carnitine deficiency and that of carnitine insufficiency was 25.3 and 86.7%, respectively.

claims.claim: Each hemodialysis session causes rapid reductions in plasma L-carnitine concentrations, and ongoing dialytic loss may slowly deplete the body pool toward a secondary deficiency.
claims.quote: Haemodialysis causes rapid reductions in plasma L-carnitine concentrations with each dialysis session.

claims.claim: The kidney maintains the endogenous carnitine pool through extensive and adaptive tubular reabsorption, so kidney disease disturbs carnitine homeostasis.
claims.quote: Among the homeostatic processes controlling the endogenous L-carnitine pool in humans, the kidney has a vital role through extensive and adaptive tubular reabsorption.

claims.claim: The 2022 Cochrane review concluded that the available evidence does not support carnitine supplementation for treating dialysis-related carnitine deficiency, while noting possible slight improvement in anaemia markers and that conclusions rest on limited data.
claims.quote: The available evidence does not currently support the use of carnitine supplementation in the treatment of dialysis-related carnitine deficiency.

claims.claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials in maintenance hemodialysis found that l-carnitine significantly decreased serum LDL and CRP but did not confirm previous findings of benefits for hemoglobin or erythropoietin dose.
claims.quote: This meta-analysis failed to confirm the previous findings regarding the effects of l-carnitine on hemoglobin and the erythropoietin dose but showed that l-carnitine significantly decreased serum LDL and CRP.

claims.claim: In a multicenter randomized controlled trial, levocarnitine therapy reduced left ventricular mass index, lowered NT-proBNP, and improved the erythropoietin responsiveness index in hemodialysis patients with left ventricular hypertrophy.
claims.quote: Levocarnitine therapy is useful for hemodialysis patients with carnitine deficiency; these patients may benefit from such therapy, with amelioration of cardiac function and reduction of left ventricular mass index.

claims.claim: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial in hemodialysis patients hyporesponsive to erythropoiesis-stimulating agents, L-carnitine reduced the erythropoietin resistance index by 25% versus 3% with placebo.
claims.quote: L-carnitine supplementation was associated with a 25% reduction in ERI, significantly greater than that seen in placebo-treated patients (3% reduction).

claims.claim: In rats subjected to renal ischemia-reperfusion, pretreatment with L-carnitine hydrochloride 100 mg/kg intraperitoneally lowered renal tissue malondialdehyde, myeloperoxidase activity, and nitrite/nitrate levels, protecting kidney tissue against ischemia-reperfusion injury.
claims.quote: It is shown that carnitine protects kidney tissue against ischaemia-reperfusion injury.

claims.claim: L-carnitine protected human HK-2 proximal tubule cells from hydrogen-peroxide-induced injury through inhibition of oxidative damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, and cell apoptosis.
claims.quote: These results suggested that L-carnitine could protect HK-2 cells from H(2)O(2)-induced injury through the inhibition of oxidative damage, mitochondria dysfunction and ultimately inhibition of cell apoptosis

claims.claim: In a clinical study of CKD patients receiving radiocontrast, carnitine pretreatment prevented the contrast-induced increase in urinary NGAL and reduced serum creatinine below basal levels.
claims.quote: In contrast, pretreatment with carnitine prevented the increase in urinary NGAL and reduced SCr below basal levels.

claims.claim: In a randomized open-label trial of 202 patients undergoing elective percutaneous coronary intervention, oral L-carnitine prevented the post-contrast rise in plasma NGAL at 12 hours.
claims.quote: Our results showed that oral L-carnitine was able to prevent an increase in NGAL following contrast medium administration in patients undergoing PCI.

claims.claim: In a double-blind randomized pilot trial in vasopressor-dependent septic shock, L-carnitine infusion appeared safe, and 28-day mortality was significantly lower in the treatment group (4 of 16 vs 9 of 15, P = .048).
claims.quote: Mortality was significantly lower at 28 days in the L-carnitine group (4/16 vs 9/15, P = .048), with a nonsignificant improved survival at 1 year (P = .06).

claims.claim: In the 250-patient phase-2 RACE adaptive randomized trial in septic shock, the most efficacious levocarnitine dose (18 g) did not meaningfully reduce cumulative organ failure at 48 hours versus placebo.
claims.quote: In this dose-finding, phase 2 adaptive randomized trial, the most efficacious dose of levocarnitine (18 g) did not meaningfully reduce cumulative organ failure at 48 hours.

claims.claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis of L-carnitine in septic shock found low-quality evidence that it has no significant effect on reducing 28-day mortality.
claims.quote: There is low-quality evidence that the use of L-carnitine has no significant effect on reducing 28-day mortality in septic shock patients.

claims.claim: A 2026 systematic review of L-carnitine and acetyl-L-carnitine in acute drug poisonings concluded that L-carnitine may be taken into consideration in severe valproate toxicity with hyperammonemia or hepatotoxicity, within thorough resuscitation protocols.
claims.quote: LC may be taken into consideration in cases of severe valproate toxicity with hyperammonemia or hepatotoxicity, as well as an adjuvant in certain organophosphate and aluminum phosphide poisonings within thorough resuscitation protocols.

claims.claim: A pilot randomized trial of oral L-carnitine around deceased-donor kidney transplantation showed no reduction in delayed graft function, although 3-month graft loss was lower in the supplemented group (1 vs 6 patients, P = .05).
claims.quote: This study showed no protective effects of oral L-carnitine supplementation against DGF occurrence recipients; however, 3-month graft loss was lower in the L-carnitine supplemented group.

claims.claim: Proximal tubules use fatty acid oxidation, which generates more ATP than glucose metabolism, as their preferred metabolic pathway to power solute reabsorption.
claims.quote: Thus, proximal tubules use fatty acid oxidation, which generates more adenosine triphosphate (ATP) than glucose metabolism, as its preferred metabolic pathway.

claims.claim: During ischemic acute renal failure, inhibition of fatty-acid beta-oxidation causes long-chain acyl carnitines and long-chain acyl coenzyme A to accumulate, and together with lysophospholipids these inhibit proximal tubule Na+K(+)-ATPase.
claims.quote: Altogether, lysophospholipids, long-chain acyl carnitines, and long-chain acyl coenzyme A inhibit proximal tubule Na+K(+)-ATPase.

claims.claim: Impairment of carnitine-induced fatty-acid oxidation contributes to diabetic kidney disease, and in a single-center randomized trial in patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis, l-carnitine supplementation preserved residual renal function and increased urine volume.
claims.quote: In our single-center randomized control trial with patients undergoing peritoneal dialysis, l-carnitine supplementation preserved residual renal function and increased urine volume, the latter of which was correlated with improvement of tubular injury.

claims.claim: In patients with septic shock, L-carnitine treatment increased levels of all measured acylcarnitines, an effect sustained for at least 36 hours after the infusion and more prominent among nonsurvivors, who had higher acylcarnitines at enrollment.
claims.quote: L-Carnitine treatment increased levels of all measured acylcarnitines; an effect that was sustained for at least 36 h following completion of the infusion and was more prominent among nonsurvivors.

claims.claim: Pro-inflammatory cytokines TNF-α, IL-1β and IFNγ downregulate OCTN2 (SLC22A5) and reduce cellular l-carnitine content through PPARγ/RXRα pathways in human colonocyte (FHC) cells.
claims.quote: Mixed proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α, IL-1β and IFNγ downregulated the expression of OCTN2 and subsequently reduced the l-Car content through PPARγ/RXRα pathways in FHC cells.

claims.claim: In septic shock, kidney-function estimates that leverage cystatin C provided the best pharmacokinetic model fit for high-dose L-carnitine, indicating renal function is a key driver of carnitine exposure in critical illness.
claims.quote: Kidney function estimates that leverage cystatin C provided superior model fit.

claims.claim: In healthy young men, urinary carnitine excretion rose 4.6-fold during five-day fasting, and the urinary excretion of carnitine increased slightly with heavy running exercise.
claims.quote: Urinary carnitine excretion was significantly increased during five-day fasting; a maximum level of 2.17 +/- 0.24 (mean and SD) mmoles/day was 4.6 times higher than the usual level of 0.47 +/- 0.10 mmoles/day (p less than 0.001).

claims.claim: In endurance athletes, six months of training lowered muscle free and total carnitine and was accompanied by significantly increased urinary excretion of esterified and total carnitine after physical exercise, changes prevented by oral L-carnitine administration.
claims.quote: These changes were likely related with the significantly increased urinary excretion of esterified and total carnitine which occurred after physical exercise.
